feature: Cooperative interruption on macOS and Windows
todo: Port cooperative interruption to macOS (SIGINT and SIGTERM) and Windows (console control events).

type_check_stubs.note: No C cross compilers here: ring's build script gets stand-ins, so these checks type-check and lint without linking.

ci.note: The branch run of the squashed changes; the TODO lines and this record were added after it.

mutation_campaign.selection: Every catalogue entry in src/interrupt.rs and src/listener.rs
oracles: cargo test --locked --test terminal_outcomes --test shutdown --test cancellation --test listeners
excluded: The Windows console handler and the macOS pipe set-up compile only on their platforms; CI runs them there in both profiles.

requirements.requirement: SIGINT and SIGTERM stop an invocation cooperatively on macOS, as on Linux
requirements.details: The signal handler counts signals and wakes a watcher thread through a pipe; macOS has no pipe2, so both ends are made close-on-exec before the CLI starts any process.

requirements.requirement: Ctrl-C and Ctrl-Break stop an invocation cooperatively on Windows
requirements.details: A console control handler, which Windows runs on a thread of its own, cancels every run and fixture through the root control and stops admission. Other console events keep their default.

requirements.requirement: A second interrupt exits at once with status 130 on every platform
requirements.details: Unix calls _exit from the signal handler; Windows terminates the process from the console handler, so neither runs destructors or flushes output another thread may hold locked. The report journal stays for reconciliation.

requirements.requirement: A listener past its close timeout has its process group killed on macOS, as on Linux
requirements.details: The group kill had been gated on Linux since listeners arrived, although every Unix starts the listener in its own group. Windows kills only the listener itself.

documentation_updates.change: Regenerated after this record added requirements.

validation_scope: Full GNU/musl debug/release suites: 2,094 tests each; strict Clippy for GNU, musl, and, type-checking without linking, macOS arm64 and Windows x86_64; formatting, coverage/mutation/performance helper checks, and the editor packages; a targeted campaign of the 8 catalogue entries in src/interrupt.rs and src/listener.rs, all caught; every test on macOS arm64 (1,993) and Windows x86_64 (1,885) in CI in each profile.
review_notes: macOS needed no new mechanism: the Linux handler was already portable POSIX apart from pipe2, so it now builds on every Unix, with the descriptors made close-on-exec by fcntl.

Windows runs a console control handler on a thread it creates, so the handler can cancel the root control and print the notice itself, where a Unix signal handler may only wake a watcher. Returning FALSE for close, logoff, and shutdown events keeps their default, which ends the process; its reports are then reconciled as after any forced termination.

Windows can deliver Ctrl-Break to one process group only, so the tests start the CLI with CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP and send GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent to that group. That also disables Ctrl-C in the child, which is why the tests send Ctrl-Break; the handler treats the two alike.
The cancellation, shutdown, and listener-group tests were gated on Linux for /proc and pipe2; they now ask ps whether a process runs and use std::io::pipe, and run on macOS too.
The catalogue entry for the second-signal mutant matched both handlers once the Windows one existed, which the catalogue check caught in CI; it now anchors on the Unix handler's _exit.
Two stale notes were corrected: getting started called Linux the only tested platform, and the worker platform page said no non-Linux backend is advertised.
limits: Closing the console window, logging off, or shutting Windows down ends the process at once, as SIGKILL does on Unix; reconcile its reports afterwards.
On Windows a listener past its close timeout is killed alone; processes it started are not.

import subprocess, json, hashlib, re, tempfile, os, sys
root=Path.cwd()

out=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="interrupts-validation-",dir=root/"target"))
print(f"validation record: {out / 'summary.json'}",flush=True)
def measured():
 inputs=[p for d in ('src','tests','examples','editors','benches','usability') for p in (root/d).rglob('*') if p.is_file() and '__pycache__' not in p.parts and 'node_modules' not in p.parts and p.suffix != '.vsix']
 inputs += sorted((root/'docs').rglob('*.md')) + sorted((root/'docs').rglob('*.schema.json')) + [root/'README.md']
 inputs += [root/'docs/performance-baseline-evidence.json', root/'docs/performance-evidence.json']
 inputs += [root/p for p in ('Cargo.toml','Cargo.lock','.cargo/mutants.toml','scripts/coverage.py','scripts/mutation_core.py','scripts/performance.py','.github/workflows/ci.yml','.gitattributes','AGENTS.md','.cargo/config.toml')]
 return {str(p.resolve().relative_to(root)):hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in sorted(inputs)}
musl_cc=str(root/'target/http-musl-toolchain/root/usr/bin/musl-gcc')
record={'complete':False,'started':datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),'revision':subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],text=True).strip(),'input_sha256':measured(),'musl_compiler':musl_cc,'checks':[]}
musl=['--target','x86_64-unknown-linux-musl']
stub_ar=str(Path(__file__).with_name('fake-ar.sh'))
stubs={'CC_aarch64_apple_darwin':'/bin/true','AR_aarch64_apple_darwin':stub_ar,'CC_x86_64_pc_windows_msvc':'/bin/true','AR_x86_64_pc_windows_msvc':stub_ar,'CARGO_TARGET_DIR':str(root/'target/cross-check')}
record['type_check_stubs']={'note':'No C cross compilers here: ring\'s build script gets stand-ins, so these checks type-check and lint without linking.','CC':'/bin/true','AR':Path(stub_ar).read_text()}
commands=[('gnu-debug-full',['cargo','test','--locked']),('gnu-release-full',['cargo','test','--locked','--release']),('musl-debug-full',['cargo','test','--locked',*musl]),('musl-release-full',['cargo','test','--locked','--release',*musl]),('clippy-gnu',['cargo','clippy','--locked','--all-targets','--','-D','warnings']),('clippy-musl',['cargo','clippy','--locked',*musl,'--all-targets','--','-D','warnings']),('format',['cargo','fmt','--all','--','--check']),('coverage-helper',['python3','tests/coverage_tools.py']),('mutation-helper',['python3','tests/mutation_tools.py']),('performance-helper',['python3','tests/performance_tools.py']),('vscode-package',['sh','-c','cd editors/vscode && npm run package']),('clippy-macos',['cargo','clippy','--locked','--target','aarch64-apple-darwin','--all-targets','--','-D','warnings']),('clippy-windows',['cargo','clippy','--locked','--target','x86_64-pc-windows-msvc','--all-targets','--','-D','warnings'])]
previous=json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text()) if len(sys.argv)>1 else None
if previous:
 assert previous['input_sha256']==record['input_sha256'], 'inputs changed since the resumed record'
 record['resumed_from']={'record':sys.argv[1],'sha256':hashlib.sha256(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'started':previous['started']}
 labels=[label for label,_ in commands]
 kept=[check for check in previous['checks'] if check['status']==0 and check['label'] in labels and [c for l,c in commands if l==check['label']][0]==check['command']]
 for check in kept:
  assert hashlib.sha256((root/check['log']).read_bytes()).hexdigest()==check['log_sha256']
 record['checks']=kept
 print('resumed', [check['label'] for check in kept], flush=True)
try:
 for label,command in commands:
  if any(check['label']==label for check in record['checks']):
   continue
  print('running '+label,flush=True)
  log=out/(label+'.log')
  with log.open('w') as stream:
   result=subprocess.run(command,stdout=stream,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,timeout=2400,env=dict(os.environ,CARGO_BUILD_JOBS='4',CC_x86_64_unknown_linux_musl=musl_cc,BOTWORK_REQUIRE_EDITORS='all',**(stubs if label in ('clippy-macos','clippy-windows') else {})))
  content=log.read_text()
  rows=re.findall(r'test result: (?:ok|FAILED)\. (\d+) passed; (\d+) failed; (\d+) ignored;',content)
  check={'label':label,'command':command,'status':result.returncode,'log':str(log.relative_to(root)),'tests':dict(zip(('passed','failed','ignored'),[sum(int(row[i]) for row in rows) for i in range(3)])),'log_sha256':hashlib.sha256(log.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}
  record['checks'].append(check)
  (out/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(record,indent=2)+'\n')
  print(json.dumps(check),flush=True)
  if result.returncode:
   print(content[-12000:],flush=True)
   raise SystemExit(result.returncode)
 record['inputs_unchanged']=measured()==record['input_sha256']
 record['complete']=record['inputs_unchanged']
finally:
 record['finished']=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
 (out/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(record,indent=2)+'\n')
print('complete' if record['complete'] else 'INPUTS CHANGED', flush=True)

"""Record a CI run's jobs: conclusions, test totals, and the results of the
interruption tests: tests/terminal_outcomes.rs, tests/cancellation.rs, and
tests/shutdown.rs on Linux and macOS, and tests/console_interrupts.rs on
Windows."""
import hashlib, json, re, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path
run, out = sys.argv[1], Path(sys.argv[2])
UNIX = ["interrupting_a_batch_gives_each_started_run_one_outcome", "interrupted_suites_tear_down_ready_fixtures_and_keep_reruns_unavailable", "a_second_interrupt_exits_at_once_and_reconciliation_marks_runs_interrupted", "forced_termination_blocks_new_reports_until_reconciled", "console_reporting_failures_keep_every_started_runs_record", "concurrent_failures_each_have_exactly_one_outcome_and_their_own_artifacts", "an_interrupted_single_file_publishes_an_interrupted_report", "interrupts_stop_cli_processes_requests_and_nested_cleanup", "deadlines_reach_cleanup_through_nested_calls_and_loops", "interrupts_reach_a_hung_listener_within_its_close_timeout", "a_destination_that_never_reads_cannot_hold_a_stopped_cli", "blocked_reads_and_preparation_end_within_the_stop_grace", "interrupts_reach_suite_cases_without_fixtures", "cleanup_failures_and_blocked_cleanup_keep_the_run_bounded", "hung_listeners_and_their_processes_are_stopped_at_the_close_timeout"]
WINDOWS = ["ctrl_break_stops_started_runs_and_publishes_an_interrupted_report", "a_second_ctrl_break_exits_at_once"]
view = json.loads(subprocess.check_output(["gh", "run", "view", run, "--json", "jobs,headSha,headBranch,conclusion"], text=True))
record = {"run": run, "url": f"https://github.com/dhilipsiva/botwork/actions/runs/{run}", "head_sha": view["headSha"], "branch": view["headBranch"], "conclusion": view["conclusion"], "jobs": {}}
for job in view["jobs"]:
    log = subprocess.check_output(["gh", "api", f"repos/dhilipsiva/botwork/actions/jobs/{job['databaseId']}/logs"], text=True)
    log = re.sub(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*m", "", re.sub(r"^\S+Z ", "", log, flags=re.M))
    rows = re.findall(r"test result: (?:ok|FAILED)\. (\d+) passed; (\d+) failed; (\d+) ignored;", log)
    entry = {"conclusion": job["conclusion"], "log_sha256": hashlib.sha256(log.encode()).hexdigest()}
    if rows:
        entry["tests"] = dict(zip(("passed", "failed", "ignored"), [sum(int(row[i]) for row in rows) for i in range(3)]))
    # Cargo's headers and the tests' results interleave in the log, so the
    # tests are matched by name.
    entry["interrupts"] = dict(re.findall(r"^test (" + "|".join(UNIX + WINDOWS) + r") \.\.\. (\w+)", log, re.M))
    record["jobs"][job["name"]] = entry
out.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n")
print(json.dumps({name: {k: v for k, v in job.items() if k != "log_sha256"} for name, job in record["jobs"].items()}, indent=1))
